newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico should unite currency with U.S. - Cavallo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico should unite currency with U.S. - Cavallo.

text.p: One of Latin America's most influential economic thinkers suggested late on Friday that Mexico unite its currency with the U.S. dollar.

"In relation to the United States, Mexico has to think twice about whether it wants to move toward a monetary union with the United States," former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said during the State of the World forum in the central Mexican city of Guanajuato.
Otherwise, he said, Mexico would find a "difficult road to economic and political progress."
Cavallo's policy of "parity" establishing a one-to-one exchange rate of the Argentine peso to U.S. dollar was widely cheered by foreign investors.
His falling out with Argentine President Carlos Menem earlier this year, leading to his dismissal, rocked financial markets throughout the Americas.
"Having a currency tied to the dollar is not losing sovereignty," Cavallo told about 500 people attending a dinner conference.

Mexican authorities were unavailable for immediate comment, but the idea is likely to be be roundly rejected in this highly nationalistic country. Should Mexico even consider the idea, it almost certainly would mean giving up the peso for the U.S. dollar.

Cavallo blasted what he said was the erroneous policy of many Latin American governments of "circulating money to influence interest rates or to alter the nominal exchange rate, which influences the relative costs of exporters."

Attempting to influence the free market through monetary policy "is an illusion that will lead us to many mistakes" in Latin America and is a course best left to the industrialised economies of the United States, Japan and the European Union, he said.
